text: This chapter has used five different DMV queries at five different moments: sessions, slow queries, missing indexes, blocking, and fragmentation. Running all five by hand every time someone complains doesn't scale, and it means you only ever look after a complaint already arrived. One view that surfaces the highest-value signals continuously changes that.

dbo dot vw_HealthDashboard combines three UNION ALL branches, one per signal this chapter diagnosed by hand: active blocking right now, expensive cached queries by average CPU, and indexes drifting back toward fragmentation. Each branch reuses exactly the DMVs from earlier lessons, nothing new to learn, just combined into one place.

A DBA checking in once a day, or an automated alert querying this view on a schedule, gets a single scannable result set instead of remembering which five queries to run and in what order. The signal column makes it immediately obvious which category a row belongs to.

Every fix in this chapter so far was reactive — a department complained, and the investigation started from there. A dashboard query checked regularly turns the same signals proactive: catching a new blocking chain or a newly fragmented index before a third department ever sends an email.

With this dashboard in place, Billing's index is fixed and maintained, Scheduling's blocking is fixed, and both are watched going forward. But that's not quite the end of the story — a new slowdown shows up next, weeks later, with no code change behind it.
